page.layout: One printed page, one text column. Running head at top left, page number at top right. Upper block in italic, running on from the previous page. Lower block in roman, two numbered paragraphs. No notes in either margin.

p.i: bus eius[?] parallelis in duas aequales partes. In reliquis climatibus, sole peruagante signa septentrionalia, dies prolixior erit nocte: sicut in oppositis signis versus meridiem nox prolixior erit die. Si autem sol maxime ab aequatore declinauerit, ut sit in principio cancri; dies erit prolixissimus, & breuissima nox. Sole peruagante signa meridionalia, dies breuior erit nocte: & quotidie quantitas diei decrescet, donec sol attingat principium capricorni: tunc erit breuissimus dies, & nox longissima. Si duo loca occurrant in duobus ex diametro oppositis parallelis: tunc arcus diurnus vnius loci aequalis erit arcui nocturno alterius, eritque dies vnius aequalis nocti alterius, & nox vnius aequabitur diei alterius: & prolixissimus dies in cancro, aequalis erit longissimae nocti in capricorno. Atque haec in genere accidunt locis habitabilibus terrae.

main_text.p: 1 Vertex capitis dicitur polus horizontis, quem corrupte nominant Zenith, cum Arabes scribant Semith: punctum verticj oppositum appellatur Nathir, quasi dicas punctum simile: est enim illud quasi alter polus horizontis, nobis depressus.

2 Postquam Altraganus per loca aequatori subiecta, naturam sphaerae rectae adumbrauit: incipit declarare situ sphaerae obliquae: in qua cum loca insignia sint, quae subiecta sunt tropico cancri, illorum proprietates prius exponit: quod scilicet in principio cancri solem habeant verticalem, & polus septentrionalis ad 23 [?] gradus & 35 [?].

page.notes: Running head and the Roman numeral in it read as CAPVT VIII; the last numeral is slightly worn. "eius" at the start is a fragment and reads uncertainly as "eins". The numbers "23" and "35" in the final line are printed with worn long-tailed figures and are marked [?]. The "2" paragraph starts at the end of a line, so it is taken as a new paragraph.
